timeline.body:
This flag mirrors `--experimental_check_output_files` to allow installations with a large number of external files to not scan them for changes on every bazel invocation.

If used in combination with `--experimental_check_output_files` and `--watchfs` you can now avoid scanning the cache for invalidations entirely allowing large projects to keep many things cached while still executing small `bazel run` commands quickly.

Fixes #14400

Setting the default the other way passes all tests: https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/pull/14415 https://buildkite.com/bazel/bazel-bazel-github-presubmit/builds/9891 so there isn't any existing test coverage for `external` files changing out from under `bazel`'s control.

cc @haxorz and you worked with `--noexperimental_check_output_files` in 60108839363 (6 years ago!) 
cc @susinmotion since you worked in here in 04dff44f530 more recently

Thinking a bit more about this, I can't see a reason why we would want to scan the filesystem for changes for anything from an `http_archive` or `git_repository`. Yes, for `local_repository` we absolutely should check the filesystem, but should I not make this a flag and instead just skip it all the time for those `bazel`-owned files?

@alexeagle pointed out that maybe scanning the file system by default is good for build reproducibility and this flag is only valuable in CI. Starting with a flag is the least impact so I guess starting here makes sense.
What about if you're using `--override_repository`? In that case does this disabling scanning for changes in those? In which case developing rule sets would be affected if you passed this

@keith yes, this would disable scanning those too since I think they would still be `EXTERNAL` files. But this flag is only intended for running `bazel` in environments where the filesystem is completely controlled by `bazel` (just like the corresponding `experimental_check_output_files `). We intend to use it in CI and not for people's local machines.

it might be nice to carve out that case if possible since then you could avoid that distinction. We use `experimental_check_output_files` for developers as well to reduce incremental build time, and would similarly like to use this if it worked well enough that someone would have to be doing something quite weird to break it.

Interesting point. I'm scared to enable it in dev as it won't guarantee
hermetic builds but I'm happy to exclude those since we obviously won't be
using them in CI.

Having said that, the main speedup here is not walking the whole cache
structure at all rather than skipping the filesystem stats so you'll lose
the speed if you have any of those overrides at all. So enabling it in dev
won't give you much.

Would the maintainers want me to set a bit if you have those and still do
the scan if they are present? I'm inclined to do that as a follow-up if
needed since that experience will be much slower.

Sorry I didn't notice this before:

Unfortunately the github PR interface doesn't let me comment on unchanged lines, but I'm a bit concerned about lines 493-498 in this PR: the guard of when to check inside handleDiffs seems to be both stricter and looser than this check. In substance, this flag seems to be inconsistently assuming that "external repository" files should count as "external" files. Do you want them to? I would naively think that you would want this flag only for external non-repository files. I don't think it should apply to both non-repository and repository files, we'd probably want separate flags. Here are the inconsistencies I see:

(1) This check doesn't respect the value of customDirtinessCheckers. I think the only place that's set is in BazelRepositoryModule, with a RepositoryDirectoryDirtinessChecker. Based on that class's javadoc, it looks like this check would lead to a bug where a `--nofetch` build followed by a `--fetch` build didn't properly update repositories when running with `--watchfs`, `--noexperimental_check_external_files` and `--noexperimental_check_output_files`.

(2) Similarly, it looks like *either* checkExternalFiles should make us ignore externalFilesKnowledge.anyFilesInExternalRepoSeen or it should be overridden. Right now, there's a redundant check, which I think you can exercise by doing a `--nowatchfs build --nobuild` on a project with a file in an external repository, then on an incremental build do `--nowatchfs build --nocheck_external_files` , and having a file in an external repository. That will do a full filesystem scan. However, running with `--watchfs` (and `--noexperimental_check_output_files`) will skip the full filesystem scan. That seems wrong. Also, anyFIlesInExternalRepoSeen can refer either to "normal" external repository files (which maybe you want to suppress checking for) and to "managed directories" (see ExternalFilesHelper) which is a pretty tricky concept. Is it actually the case that you want to disable checks in managed directories with this flag, even if you do want to suppress repository checks? I think probably not, although I'm not positive when managed directories are expected to be updated by the corresponding repository rules. If you don't want to disable such checks, you'll probably need to split the ExternalFilesKnowledge boolean into two, and track them separately in ExternalFilesHelper.

It sounds like this flag is only intended for external *repositories*, not external files in general. In that case, I have a few suggestions. First, change the name to experimental_check_external_repository_files. Second, move the flag to RepositoryOptions. You can still access it in SequencedSkyframeExecutor via the `options` variable.

About the test cases, for (1) the --fetch flag seems to be in a pretty sorry state, so I'm not sure what the semantics actually are right now, and I don't know that it's worth digging too much deeper. My suspicion is that something else is causing invalidation (maybe a transient error). You might be able to trigger it by having a repository that is fetched, but then is updated to a new version and the build is run with --nofetch, so the updated version isn't actually used. But I'm not positive. Any Google folks who actually maintain this functionality are welcome to weigh in. Maybe @Wyverald knows?

For (2), I think that you *don't* want to affect the checks for external files that are not in repositories. That specifically means that ExternalFilesKnowledge#tooManyNonOutputExternalFilesSeen and ExternalFilesKnowledge#tooManyNonOutputExternalFilesSeen#nonOutputExternalFilesSeen should not be connected to your flag at all. You can enforce that in a test by just creating a symlink to a random other file on disk, modifying the file, and verifying that we rebuild even with all checks disabled.

timeline.message:
Add `--experimental_check_external_repository_files`

This flag mirrors `--experimental_check_output_files` to allow installations
with a large number of external files to not scan them for changes on
every bazel invocation.

If used in combination with `--experimental_check_output_files` and
`--watchfs` you can now avoid scanning the filesystem entirely allowing
large projects to keep many things cached while still executing small
`bazel run` commands quickly.

Fixes #14400

+    --noexperimental_check_external_repository_files \

+    --watchfs \
+    @remote//:g >& "$TEST_log" && fail "Expected build to fail" || true
+  expect_log "no such package '@bazel_tools//tools/build_defs/repo'"
+  bazel build \
+    --fetch \
+    --noexperimental_check_external_repository_files \
+    --noexperimental_check_output_files \
+    --watchfs \
+    @remote//:g >& "$TEST_log" || fail "Expected build to pass"
+}
+
+test_no_build_doesnt_break_the_cache() {
+  setup_remote
+  bazel build \
+    --nobuild \
+    --noexperimental_check_external_repository_files \
+    --noexperimental_check_output_files \
+    --watchfs \
+    @remote//:g >& "$TEST_log" || fail "Expected build to pass"
+  [[ ! -f bazel-main/external/remote/BUILD ]] || fail "external files shouldn't have been made"
+  bazel build \
+    --noexperimental_check_external_repository_files \
+    --noexperimental_check_output_files \
+    --watchfs \
+    @remote//:g >& "$TEST_log" || fail "Expected build to pass"
+}
+
+test_symlink_outside_still_checked() {
+  mkdir main
+  cd main
+  create_workspace_with_default_repos WORKSPACE
+  echo 'sh_test(name = "symlink", srcs = ["symlink.sh"])' > BUILD
+
+  mkdir ../foo
+  echo 'exit 0' > ../foo/foo.sh
+  chmod u+x ../foo/foo.sh
+  ln -s ../foo/foo.sh symlink.sh
+
+  bazel test \
+    --noexperimental_check_external_repository_files \
+    --noexperimental_check_output_files \
+    --watchfs \
+    :symlink >& "$TEST_log" || fail "Expected build to succeed"
+
+  bazel test \
+    --noexperimental_check_external_repository_files \
+    --noexperimental_check_output_files \
+    --watchfs \
+    :symlink >& "$TEST_log" || fail "Expected build to succeed"
+  expect_log '//:symlink.*cached'
+
+  echo 'exit 1' > ../foo/foo.sh
+
+  bazel test \
+    --noexperimental_check_external_repository_files \
+    --noexperimental_check_output_files \
+    --watchfs \
+    :symlink >& "$TEST_log" && fail "Expected build to fail" || true
+  expect_not_log '//:symlink.*cached'
+  expect_log '1 test FAILED'
+}
+
+run_suite "check_external_files tests"
